clue.text: Clear area in quiet part of camp

indicators.note: one thing set in another is placed inside it, so the area letter goes within the next item

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
standard abbreviation for area
a tent is one part of a camp

explanation.surface: Someone clears a patch of ground in a quiet corner of a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside P, then TENT follows: P(A)TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or plainly evident, a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Fast mover, or one barely running

blocks.note: first meaning: something that streaks along at speed
second meaning: a person who runs naked through a public place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' is the pun: it means almost not, but here it means without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both anything that moves at great speed and a naked runner who dashes across a sports pitch or crowd.

clue.text: A truce I arranged, including individual who has lots to offer?

definitions.note: elliptical: read as 'one who has lots to offer'

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put into a new order
something including another item holds it within itself

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an individual is one

explanation.surface: A negotiated truce brings in someone with plenty to give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' are the numbered items sold at a sale, not a large quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer offers lots, the numbered items, to bidders at a sale.

clue.text: After crazy rising, people getting endless punishment

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises is read from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: mad means crazy
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A population suffers unending punishment after a bout of mad unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' is part of the definition, not a signal to drop a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is the eternal punishment of the soul in hell, so it is punishment without end.

clue.text: Fit for second or last part in Shakespeare play

definitions.text: second or last part in Shakespeare play

blocks.note: first meaning: healthy, in good shape

blocks.clueFragment: second or last part in Shakespeare play
blocks.note: second meaning: the second and final word of the title All's ___ That Ends ___

explanation.walkthrough: The Shakespeare comedy All's Well That Ends Well has the same word second and last in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Well means healthy or fit, and it is the word repeated in the title All's Well That Ends Well.

clue.text: A wife in one African country or another

indicators.note: something put in another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
taken as written
standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife lives in some African country, one or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' is the whole definition, meaning a second African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa, so it is a second African country.

clue.text: Doctor deviates, producing remedy for nerves

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the following letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor departs from standard practice and prescribes something for anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician prescribing, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a drug that calms a person and soothes anxiety.

clue.text: One thing we hear about time that's surprise

indicators.note: a word about another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: a means one
a sound is something heard
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Some noise heard at a particular moment comes as a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze or take aback, a synonym of the verb surprise.

clue.text: Give everyone a hand in agreement

blocks.note: first meaning: distribute cards to every player
second meaning: a bargain or arrangement

explanation.walkthrough: 'Give everyone a hand' sounds like helping or applauding, but it is about handing out playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal is to share out cards so each player holds a hand, and a deal is also a settled agreement.

clue.text: State how old someone is? That could be mean

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
age is how old someone is

explanation.surface: Asking someone their age might seem unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like unkind, but it is the arithmetical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the average, the sum of the values divided by their count.

clue.text: Problem for readers, I agree, in English school

indicators.note: something in something else sits inside it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for English
to school someone is to train them
yes is what you say when you agree

explanation.surface: A pupil at an English school agrees that reading causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a verb here, meaning to instruct, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye strain is fatigue of the eyes, a common complaint among those who read for long periods.

clue.text: Climber in Australian Alps

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is scaling the Australian Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer in the Alps; it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests, so a climbing plant.

clue.text: Also including thousand yen in capital where it's usable

indicators.note: something including other items holds them inside itself

blocks.note: too means also
k stands for a thousand
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A thousand yen can also be spent in the city where that currency works.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' of the definition is the yen, Japan's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital of Japan, whose currency is the yen.

clue.text: Where journeys end, in theory — oddly, by car

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd-numbered positions only
by means beside, so one piece is placed next to the other

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters
the Mini is a classic British small car

explanation.surface: In theory, journeys end strangely when made by car.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end stations of railway or bus routes, the plural of terminus.

clue.text: Presenter of show in the round starring me in new production

definitions.text: Presenter of show in the round

indicators.note: a new production restages the material, so these letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre-in-the-round presenter announces a new show starring himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the round' looks like theatre staging, but it describes a circus ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringmaster introduces the acts in a circus, which is performed in a circular ring.

clue.text: Sabotage how James Bond worked in East

blocks.note: Bond works under M, the head of the Secret Service in the novels and films
taken as written
standard abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A spy is asked how James Bond carried out sabotage in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the code name of James Bond's boss, so Bond worked 'under M'.
explanation.definitionFit: To undermine is to weaken something covertly, an act of sabotage.

clue.text: Queen who made herself unpopular, namely in dreadful rant at one time

indicators.note: something dreadful is a mess, so the following letters are jumbled
something in another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
i.e. (id est) means namely

explanation.surface: A queen became hated after a dreadful outburst long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At one time' feels like a time phrase, but it is all anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Antoinette, queen of France, was widely loathed before the Revolution and was guillotined in 1793.

clue.text: Medic declined to cover condition that's changed

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: MO is Medical Officer
declined in the sense of faded away and died
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A doctor refused to treat an illness that has altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declined' looks like refused, but means sank and passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Modified means altered or adjusted, so a synonym of changed.

clue.text: Secured by rope, some frigate there docked

indicators.note: some means only a part of the words that follow is taken

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A warship tied up at the quay where it docked.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied with a rope or chain so it cannot move away.

clue.text: I had turned over poems of various kinds

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped, so its letters run the other way

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone recalls leafing through a varied collection of poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse means varied, showing many different types.

clue.text: Destructive type in museum then left

blocks.note: the V and A, the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A wrecker got into a museum and then departed.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A, spelt out as V AND A, is the Victoria and Albert Museum, a major London museum of art and design.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal deliberately damages property, a person bent on destruction.

clue.text: For example, lead guest finally into dinner, say

definitions.note: lead is an example of the answer

indicators.note: finally takes just the closing letter of the word before it
one thing put into another goes inside it

blocks.note: dinner is an example of a meal
final letter

explanation.surface: A host leads the guest last into the dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the verb to guide, but it is the heavy element.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a heavy metallic element, so an example of a metal.

clue.text: Like Hawaii as state, or Louisiana, on trial

blocks.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Hawaii and Louisiana are both put on trial as states.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts LA above TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii was the fiftieth and most recent state to join the United States, in 1959.

clue.text: Swindle, i.e. something that's not on the level

definitions.text: something that's not on the level

blocks.note: first meaning: a dishonest scheme, a racket

blocks.clueFragment: something that's not on the level
blocks.note: second meaning: a sloping surface joining two heights

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on the level' is the idiom for dishonest, which seems to repeat 'swindle', but here it means sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is an inclined slope between levels, and in British slang a fraudulent racket.

clue.text: Big game found, if not actually lions initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A safari found big game, though not actually lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' suggests safari animals; it is the deciding match of a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A final is the climactic match of a tournament, the biggest game of the season.

clue.text: Placed face up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Something is put down with its face turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, meaning put down or placed.

clue.text: Check on eligibility for aid statesmen revised

indicators.note: something revised is reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Politicians have rewritten the rules on who qualifies for state help.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test assesses someone's income and assets to decide whether they qualify for state benefits.

clue.text: Family member, right from the start, in euphoric state

indicators.note: taking a letter from the start removes it from the front of the word

blocks.note: a relation is a family member
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A relative, right from the beginning, is overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right from the start' reads as 'from the very beginning', but it tells you to take R off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness and exhilaration, a euphoric condition.

clue.text: Lady, perhaps, showing journalists around borders of estate

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, first and last
something placed around another surrounds it

blocks.note: the press is journalists collectively
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Reporters are shown around the edges of an aristocrat's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress holds a title in the peerage, and Lady is a form of address for one, hence the 'perhaps'.
